status_summary: Proclamation 10886 (signed 2025-01-20) declared a national emergency at the southern border and directed military support, additional physical barriers and a 90-day report, while Proclamation 10888 and Executive Order 14165 of the same date suspended entry and asylum claims for people crossing the border, directed resumption of Remain in Mexico and called for an end to catch-and-release. A federal district court ruled on 2025-07-02 that the asylum shutdown was unlawful and a D.C. Circuit panel affirmed on 2026-04-24; the mandate is stayed and the government petitioned the Supreme Court on 2026-08-24 (conference 2026-11-06), and SCOTUSblog reports that the stay lets the asylum restrictions remain in place for now. A DHS and CBP release dated 2026-05-15 states that April 2026 was the twelfth consecutive month of zero Border Patrol releases at the border and gives 8,943 Southwest border apprehensions for April, a daily average of 298 and 215,876 fiscal-year-to-date CBP encounters (agency claims, not independently verified), and a Fox News report of 2026-09-16 citing agency figures describes a sixteenth consecutive month of zero releases, with 8,870 Southwest border Border Patrol apprehensions in August 2026, and a DHS release of 2026-10-16 gives preliminary fiscal year 2026 figures of 98,708 Southwest border Border Patrol apprehensions and 379,243 nationwide encounters and calls September the seventeenth consecutive month of zero releases (agency claims, not independently verified). The border is not sealed in the Foreword's sense and illegal immigration is not ended, but enforcement at the border is operative.

timeline.event: President signs Proclamation 10886 declaring a national emergency at the southern border (published 2025-01-29): it directs the military to support DHS in gaining operational control, directs additional physical barriers, and requires a 90-day Defense and DHS report on conditions including whether to invoke the Insurrection Act.

Proclamation 10888 suspends entry of people it describes as engaged in an invasion across the southern border and bars them from invoking asylum and related provisions; Executive Order 14165 of the same date directs DHS to resume Migrant Protection Protocols, to detain apprehended people to the extent permitted by law and to end the practice known as catch-and-release.

In RAICES v. Noem the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia grants summary judgment to the plaintiffs in part and certifies a class, holding that Proclamation 10888 and its implementing guidance violated the INA; on 2025-08-01 the D.C. Circuit dissolves its administrative stay and grants the government's stay motion in part.
A divided D.C. Circuit panel affirms the summary judgment and class certification in RAICES v. Noem (174 F.4th 81); rehearing en banc is denied 2026-07-23 and the mandate is stayed on 2026-07-27.

DHS and CBP release a statement that April 2026 was the twelfth consecutive month of zero Border Patrol releases at the border, with 8,943 Southwest border apprehensions in April and a daily average of 298; these are the agency's own figures and comparisons, not independently verified. The release shows no date line; the date comes from the page address.

The Solicitor General files a petition for certiorari in Mullin v. RAICES (No. 26-239); the respondents' brief was filed 2026-09-23, the reply 2026-10-06, and the case was distributed on 2026-10-07 for the 2026-11-06 conference.

timeline.event: A Fox News report citing a DHS and CBP statement gives 8,870 Southwest border Border Patrol apprehensions in August 2026 (5 percent below July) and a 16th consecutive month of zero releases; these are agency figures, not independently verified.

DHS announces preliminary fiscal year 2026 DHS and CBP border data: 98,708 Southwest border apprehensions by the Border Patrol (which the release calls a 95 percent decline from more than 1.8 million a year under the prior administration), 379,243 total nationwide encounters (called the lowest in agency history), what it calls the first fiscal year with zero Border Patrol releases, with September the 17th consecutive month of zero releases, 250 miles of new border barrier completed since 2025-01-20 and nearly 1 million pounds of drugs seized; the release quotes Secretary Markwayne Mullin and CBP Commissioner Rodney S. Scott. These are the agency's own preliminary figures, not independently verified.
